8	### Properties of the models relation for setoid algebras
9	
10	We prove some closure and invariance properties of the relation `⊧`.  In particular, we prove the following facts (which are needed, for example, in the proof the Birkhoff HSP Theorem).
11	
12	* [Algebraic invariance](#algebraic-invariance). `⊧` is an *algebraic invariant* (stable under isomorphism).

16	* [Product invariance](#product-invariance). Identities modeled by a class of algebras are also modeled by all products of algebras in the class.

59	
60	#### Algebraic invariance of ⊧ {#algebraic-invariance}
61	
62	The binary relation ⊧ would be practically useless if it were not an *algebraic invariant* (i.e., invariant under isomorphism).
63	
64	
65	```agda
66	module _ {X : Type χ}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}(𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ)(p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X) where
67	  open Environment 𝑨      using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧   to ⟦_⟧₁ )
68	  open Environment 𝑩      using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧   to ⟦_⟧₂ )
69	  open Setoid (Domain 𝑩)  using ( _≈_ ; sym ; trans )
70	  open SetoidReasoning (Domain 𝑩)
71	
72	  ⊧-I-invar : 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)  →  𝑨 ≅ 𝑩  →  𝑩 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
73	  ⊧-I-invar Apq (mkiso fh gh f∼g g∼f) ρ = trans i $ trans ii $ trans iii $ trans iv v
74	    where
75	    -- TODO: refactor this proof using new relational reasoning syntax/style
76	    f = _⟨$⟩_ (proj₁ fh) ; g = _⟨$⟩_ (proj₁ gh)
77	
78	    i : ⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ ρ ≈ ⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (f ∘ (g ∘ ρ))
79	    i = sym $ cong ⟦ p ⟧₂ (f∼g ∘ ρ)
80	
81	    ii : ⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (f ∘ (g ∘ ρ)) ≈ f (⟦ p ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (g ∘ ρ))
82	    ii = sym $ comm-hom-term fh p (g ∘ ρ)
83	
84	    iii : f (⟦ p ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (g ∘ ρ)) ≈ f (⟦ q ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (g ∘ ρ))
85	    iii = cong (proj₁ fh) $ Apq (g ∘ ρ)
86	
87	    iv : f (⟦ q ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (g ∘ ρ)) ≈ ⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (f ∘ (g ∘ ρ))
88	    iv = comm-hom-term fh q (g ∘ ρ)
89	
90	    v : ⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (f ∘ (g ∘ ρ)) ≈ ⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ ρ
91	    v = cong ⟦ q ⟧₂ (f∼g ∘ ρ)
92	```
93	
94	
95	As the proof makes clear, we show `𝑩 ⊧ p ≈ q` by showing that `𝑩 ⟦ p ⟧ ≡ 𝑩 ⟦ q ⟧`
96	holds *extensionally*, that is, `∀ x, 𝑩 ⟦ p ⟧ x ≡ 𝑩 ⟦q ⟧ x`.
97	
98	#### Lift-invariance of ⊧ {#lift-invariance}
99	The ⊧ relation is also invariant under the algebraic lift and lower operations.
100	
101	
102	```agda
103	module _ {X : Type χ}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ} where
104	
105	  ⊧-Lift-invar : (p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X) → 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q) → Lift-Algˡ 𝑨 β ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
106	  ⊧-Lift-invar p q Apq = ⊧-I-invar (Lift-Algˡ 𝑨 _) p q Apq Lift-≅ˡ
107	
108	  ⊧-lower-invar : (p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X) → Lift-Algˡ 𝑨 β ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)  →  𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
109	  ⊧-lower-invar p q lApq = ⊧-I-invar 𝑨 p q lApq (≅-sym Lift-≅ˡ)
110	```
111	
112	
113	#### Homomorphic invariance of ⊧
114	Identities modeled by an algebra `𝑨` are also modeled by every homomorphic image
115	of `𝑨`, which fact can be formalized as follows.
116	
117	
118	```agda
119	module _ {X : Type χ}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ}{p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X} where
120	
121	  ⊧-H-invar : 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q) → 𝑩 IsHomImageOf 𝑨 → 𝑩 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
122	  ⊧-H-invar Apq (φh , φE) ρ =
123	   begin
124	        ⟦ p ⟧   ⟨$⟩               ρ    ≈˘⟨  cong ⟦ p ⟧(λ _ → InvIsInverseʳ φE)  ⟩
125	        ⟦ p ⟧   ⟨$⟩ (φ ∘  φ⁻¹  ∘  ρ)   ≈˘⟨  comm-hom-term φh p (φ⁻¹ ∘ ρ)        ⟩
126	    φ(  ⟦ p ⟧ᴬ  ⟨$⟩ (     φ⁻¹  ∘  ρ))  ≈⟨   cong (proj₁ φh) (Apq (φ⁻¹ ∘ ρ))         ⟩
127	    φ(  ⟦ q ⟧ᴬ  ⟨$⟩ (     φ⁻¹  ∘  ρ))  ≈⟨   comm-hom-term φh q (φ⁻¹ ∘ ρ)        ⟩
128	        ⟦ q ⟧   ⟨$⟩ (φ ∘  φ⁻¹  ∘  ρ)   ≈⟨   cong ⟦ q ⟧(λ _ → InvIsInverseʳ φE)  ⟩
129	        ⟦ q ⟧   ⟨$⟩               ρ    ∎
130	    where
131	    φ⁻¹ : 𝕌[ 𝑩 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑨 ]
132	    φ⁻¹ = SurjInv (proj₁ φh) φE
133	    φ = (_⟨$⟩_ (proj₁ φh))
134	    open Environment 𝑨  using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧ to ⟦_⟧ᴬ)
135	    open Environment 𝑩  using ( ⟦_⟧ )
136	    open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑩 ]
137	```
138	
139	
140	
141	#### Subalgebraic invariance of ⊧ {#subalgebraic-invariance}
142	Identities modeled by an algebra `𝑨` are also modeled by every subalgebra of `𝑨`, which fact can be formalized as follows.
143	
144	
145	```agda
146	module _ {X : Type χ}{p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ} where
147	  open Environment 𝑨      using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧ to ⟦_⟧₁ )
148	  open Environment 𝑩      using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧ to ⟦_⟧₂ )
149	  open Setoid (Domain 𝑨)  using ( _≈_ )
150	  open Setoid (Domain 𝑩)  using () renaming ( _≈_ to _≈₂_ )
151	  open SetoidReasoning (Domain 𝑨)
152	
153	  ⊧-S-invar : 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q) →  𝑩 ≤ 𝑨  →  𝑩 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
154	  ⊧-S-invar Apq B≤A b = goal
155	    where
156	    hh : hom 𝑩 𝑨
157	    hh = (proj₁ B≤A)
158	    h = _⟨$⟩_ (proj₁ hh)
159	    ξ : ∀ b → h (⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b) ≈ h (⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b)
160	    ξ b = begin
161	           h (⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b)    ≈⟨ comm-hom-term hh p b ⟩
162	           ⟦ p ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (h ∘ b)  ≈⟨ Apq (h ∘ b) ⟩
163	           ⟦ q ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (h ∘ b)  ≈˘⟨ comm-hom-term hh q b ⟩
164	           h (⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b)    ∎
165	
166	    goal : ⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b ≈₂ ⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b
167	    goal = (proj₂ B≤A) (ξ b)
168	```
169	
170	
171	Next, identities modeled by a class of algebras is also modeled by all subalgebras
172	of the class.  In other terms, every term equation `(p ≈̇ q)` that is satisfied by
173	all `𝑨 ∈ 𝒦` is also satisfied by every subalgebra of a member of `𝒦`.
174	
175	
176	```agda
177	module _ {X : Type χ}{p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X} where
178	
179	  ⊧-S-class-invar :  {𝒦 : Pred (Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ) ℓ}
180	   →                 (𝒦 ⊫ (p ≈̇ q)) → ((𝑩 , _) : SubalgebrasOfClass 𝒦 {β}{ρᵇ})
181	   →                 𝑩 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
182	  ⊧-S-class-invar Kpq (𝑩 , 𝑨 , kA , B≤A) = ⊧-S-invar{p = p}{q} (Kpq .⊫-proof 𝑨 kA) B≤A
183	```
184	
185	
186	
187	#### Product invariance of ⊧ {#product-invariance}
188	
189	An identity satisfied by all algebras in an indexed collection is also satisfied
190	by the product of algebras in that collection.
191	
192	
193	```agda
194	module _ {X : Type χ}{p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X}{I : Type ℓ}(𝒜 : I → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ) where
195	
196	  ⊧-P-invar : (∀ i → 𝒜 i ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)) → ⨅ 𝒜 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
197	  ⊧-P-invar 𝒜pq a = goal
198	    where
199	    open Algebra (⨅ 𝒜)      using () renaming ( Domain to ⨅A )
200	    open Environment (⨅ 𝒜)  using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧ to ⟦_⟧₁ )
201	    open Environment        using ( ⟦_⟧ )
202	    open Setoid ⨅A          using ( _≈_ )
203	    open SetoidReasoning ⨅A
204	
205	    ξ : (λ i → (⟦ 𝒜 i ⟧ p) ⟨$⟩ (λ x → (a x) i)) ≈ (λ i → (⟦ 𝒜 i ⟧ q) ⟨$⟩ (λ x → (a x) i))
206	    ξ = λ i → 𝒜pq i (λ x → (a x) i)
207	    goal : ⟦ p ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ a ≈ ⟦ q ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ a
208	    goal = begin
209	            ⟦ p ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ a                             ≈⟨ interp-prod 𝒜 p a ⟩
210	            (λ i → (⟦ 𝒜 i ⟧ p) ⟨$⟩ (λ x → (a x) i))  ≈⟨ ξ ⟩
211	            (λ i → (⟦ 𝒜 i ⟧ q) ⟨$⟩ (λ x → (a x) i))  ≈˘⟨ interp-prod 𝒜 q a ⟩
212	            ⟦ q ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ a                             ∎
213	```
214	
215	
216	An identity satisfied by all algebras in a class is also satisfied by the product
217	of algebras in the class.
218	
219	
220	```agda
221	  ⊧-P-class-invar :  (𝒦 : Pred (Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ)(ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} α))
222	   →                 𝒦 ⊫ (p ≈̇ q) → (∀ i → 𝒜 i ∈ 𝒦) → ⨅ 𝒜 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
223	
224	  ⊧-P-class-invar 𝒦 σ K𝒜 = ⊧-P-invar (λ i ρ → σ .⊫-proof (𝒜 i) (K𝒜 i) ρ)
225	```
226	
227	
228	Another fact that will turn out to be useful is that a product of a collection of
229	algebras models (p ≈̇ q) if the lift of each algebra in the collection models
230	(p ≈̇ q).
231	
232	
233	```agda
234	  ⊧-P-lift-invar : (∀ i → Lift-Algˡ (𝒜 i) β ⊧ (p ≈̇ q))  →  ⨅ 𝒜 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
235	  ⊧-P-lift-invar α = ⊧-P-invar Aipq
236	    where
237	    Aipq : ∀ i → (𝒜 i) ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
238	    Aipq i = ⊧-lower-invar{𝑨 = (𝒜 i)} p q (α i)
239	```
240	
241	
242	
243	#### Modeled identities and homomorphism kernels
244	
245	If an algebra 𝑨 models an identity (p ≈̇ q), then the pair (p , q) belongs to the
246	kernel of every homomorphism φ : hom (𝑻 X) 𝑨 from the term algebra to 𝑨; that is,
247	every homomorphism from 𝑻 X to 𝑨 maps p and q to the same element of 𝑨.
248	
249	 
250	```agda
251	module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥}{X : Type χ}{p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}(φh : hom (𝑻 X) 𝑨) where
252	  open Setoid (Domain 𝑨) using ( _≈_ )
253	  private φ = _⟨$⟩_ (proj₁ φh)
254	
255	  ⊧-H-ker : 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q) → φ p ≈ φ q
256	  ⊧-H-ker β =
257	   begin
258	    φ p                 ≈⟨ cong (proj₁ φh) (term-agreement p)⟩
259	    φ (⟦ p ⟧ ⟨$⟩ ℊ)     ≈⟨ comm-hom-term φh p ℊ ⟩
260	    ⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (φ ∘ ℊ)  ≈⟨ β (φ ∘ ℊ) ⟩
261	    ⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (φ ∘ ℊ)  ≈˘⟨ comm-hom-term φh q ℊ ⟩
262	    φ (⟦ q ⟧ ⟨$⟩ ℊ)     ≈˘⟨ cong (proj₁ φh) (term-agreement q)⟩
263	    φ q                 ∎
264	
265	    where
266	    open SetoidReasoning (Domain 𝑨)
267	    open Environment 𝑨      using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧ to ⟦_⟧₂ )
268	    open Environment (𝑻 X)  using ( ⟦_⟧ )
269	```

-->



#### Algebraic invariance of ⊧ {#algebraic-invariance}

The binary relation ⊧ would be practically useless if it were not an *algebraic invariant* (i.e., invariant under isomorphism).


```agda
module _ {X : Type χ}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}(𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ)(p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X) where
  open Environment 𝑨      using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧   to ⟦_⟧₁ )
  open Environment 𝑩      using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧   to ⟦_⟧₂ )
  open Setoid (Domain 𝑩)  using ( _≈_ ; sym ; trans )
  open SetoidReasoning (Domain 𝑩)

  ⊧-I-invar : 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)  →  𝑨 ≅ 𝑩  →  𝑩 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
  ⊧-I-invar Apq (mkiso fh gh f∼g g∼f) ρ = trans i $ trans ii $ trans iii $ trans iv v
    where
    -- TODO: refactor this proof using new relational reasoning syntax/style
    f = _⟨$⟩_ (proj₁ fh) ; g = _⟨$⟩_ (proj₁ gh)

    i : ⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ ρ ≈ ⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (f ∘ (g ∘ ρ))
    i = sym $ cong ⟦ p ⟧₂ (f∼g ∘ ρ)

    ii : ⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (f ∘ (g ∘ ρ)) ≈ f (⟦ p ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (g ∘ ρ))
    ii = sym $ comm-hom-term fh p (g ∘ ρ)

    iii : f (⟦ p ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (g ∘ ρ)) ≈ f (⟦ q ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (g ∘ ρ))
    iii = cong (proj₁ fh) $ Apq (g ∘ ρ)

    iv : f (⟦ q ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (g ∘ ρ)) ≈ ⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (f ∘ (g ∘ ρ))
    iv = comm-hom-term fh q (g ∘ ρ)

    v : ⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (f ∘ (g ∘ ρ)) ≈ ⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ ρ
    v = cong ⟦ q ⟧₂ (f∼g ∘ ρ)
```


As the proof makes clear, we show `𝑩 ⊧ p ≈ q` by showing that `𝑩 ⟦ p ⟧ ≡ 𝑩 ⟦ q ⟧`
holds *extensionally*, that is, `∀ x, 𝑩 ⟦ p ⟧ x ≡ 𝑩 ⟦q ⟧ x`.

#### Lift-invariance of ⊧ {#lift-invariance}
The ⊧ relation is also invariant under the algebraic lift and lower operations.


```agda
module _ {X : Type χ}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ} where

  ⊧-Lift-invar : (p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X) → 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q) → Lift-Algˡ 𝑨 β ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
  ⊧-Lift-invar p q Apq = ⊧-I-invar (Lift-Algˡ 𝑨 _) p q Apq Lift-≅ˡ

  ⊧-lower-invar : (p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X) → Lift-Algˡ 𝑨 β ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)  →  𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
  ⊧-lower-invar p q lApq = ⊧-I-invar 𝑨 p q lApq (≅-sym Lift-≅ˡ)
```


#### Homomorphic invariance of ⊧
Identities modeled by an algebra `𝑨` are also modeled by every homomorphic image
of `𝑨`, which fact can be formalized as follows.


```agda
module _ {X : Type χ}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ}{p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X} where

  ⊧-H-invar : 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q) → 𝑩 IsHomImageOf 𝑨 → 𝑩 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
  ⊧-H-invar Apq (φh , φE) ρ =
   begin
        ⟦ p ⟧   ⟨$⟩               ρ    ≈˘⟨  cong ⟦ p ⟧(λ _ → InvIsInverseʳ φE)  ⟩
        ⟦ p ⟧   ⟨$⟩ (φ ∘  φ⁻¹  ∘  ρ)   ≈˘⟨  comm-hom-term φh p (φ⁻¹ ∘ ρ)        ⟩
    φ(  ⟦ p ⟧ᴬ  ⟨$⟩ (     φ⁻¹  ∘  ρ))  ≈⟨   cong (proj₁ φh) (Apq (φ⁻¹ ∘ ρ))         ⟩
    φ(  ⟦ q ⟧ᴬ  ⟨$⟩ (     φ⁻¹  ∘  ρ))  ≈⟨   comm-hom-term φh q (φ⁻¹ ∘ ρ)        ⟩
        ⟦ q ⟧   ⟨$⟩ (φ ∘  φ⁻¹  ∘  ρ)   ≈⟨   cong ⟦ q ⟧(λ _ → InvIsInverseʳ φE)  ⟩
        ⟦ q ⟧   ⟨$⟩               ρ    ∎
    where
    φ⁻¹ : 𝕌[ 𝑩 ] → 𝕌[ 𝑨 ]
    φ⁻¹ = SurjInv (proj₁ φh) φE
    φ = (_⟨$⟩_ (proj₁ φh))
    open Environment 𝑨  using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧ to ⟦_⟧ᴬ)
    open Environment 𝑩  using ( ⟦_⟧ )
    open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑩 ]
```



#### Subalgebraic invariance of ⊧ {#subalgebraic-invariance}
Identities modeled by an algebra `𝑨` are also modeled by every subalgebra of `𝑨`, which fact can be formalized as follows.


```agda
module _ {X : Type χ}{p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}{𝑩 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} β ρᵇ} where
  open Environment 𝑨      using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧ to ⟦_⟧₁ )
  open Environment 𝑩      using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧ to ⟦_⟧₂ )
  open Setoid (Domain 𝑨)  using ( _≈_ )
  open Setoid (Domain 𝑩)  using () renaming ( _≈_ to _≈₂_ )
  open SetoidReasoning (Domain 𝑨)

  ⊧-S-invar : 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q) →  𝑩 ≤ 𝑨  →  𝑩 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
  ⊧-S-invar Apq B≤A b = goal
    where
    hh : hom 𝑩 𝑨
    hh = (proj₁ B≤A)
    h = _⟨$⟩_ (proj₁ hh)
    ξ : ∀ b → h (⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b) ≈ h (⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b)
    ξ b = begin
           h (⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b)    ≈⟨ comm-hom-term hh p b ⟩
           ⟦ p ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (h ∘ b)  ≈⟨ Apq (h ∘ b) ⟩
           ⟦ q ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ (h ∘ b)  ≈˘⟨ comm-hom-term hh q b ⟩
           h (⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b)    ∎

    goal : ⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b ≈₂ ⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ b
    goal = (proj₂ B≤A) (ξ b)
```


Next, identities modeled by a class of algebras is also modeled by all subalgebras
of the class.  In other terms, every term equation `(p ≈̇ q)` that is satisfied by
all `𝑨 ∈ 𝒦` is also satisfied by every subalgebra of a member of `𝒦`.


```agda
module _ {X : Type χ}{p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X} where

  ⊧-S-class-invar :  {𝒦 : Pred (Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ) ℓ}
   →                 (𝒦 ⊫ (p ≈̇ q)) → ((𝑩 , _) : SubalgebrasOfClass 𝒦 {β}{ρᵇ})
   →                 𝑩 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
  ⊧-S-class-invar Kpq (𝑩 , 𝑨 , kA , B≤A) = ⊧-S-invar{p = p}{q} (Kpq .⊫-proof 𝑨 kA) B≤A
```



#### Product invariance of ⊧ {#product-invariance}

An identity satisfied by all algebras in an indexed collection is also satisfied
by the product of algebras in that collection.


```agda
module _ {X : Type χ}{p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X}{I : Type ℓ}(𝒜 : I → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ) where

  ⊧-P-invar : (∀ i → 𝒜 i ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)) → ⨅ 𝒜 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
  ⊧-P-invar 𝒜pq a = goal
    where
    open Algebra (⨅ 𝒜)      using () renaming ( Domain to ⨅A )
    open Environment (⨅ 𝒜)  using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧ to ⟦_⟧₁ )
    open Environment        using ( ⟦_⟧ )
    open Setoid ⨅A          using ( _≈_ )
    open SetoidReasoning ⨅A

    ξ : (λ i → (⟦ 𝒜 i ⟧ p) ⟨$⟩ (λ x → (a x) i)) ≈ (λ i → (⟦ 𝒜 i ⟧ q) ⟨$⟩ (λ x → (a x) i))
    ξ = λ i → 𝒜pq i (λ x → (a x) i)
    goal : ⟦ p ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ a ≈ ⟦ q ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ a
    goal = begin
            ⟦ p ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ a                             ≈⟨ interp-prod 𝒜 p a ⟩
            (λ i → (⟦ 𝒜 i ⟧ p) ⟨$⟩ (λ x → (a x) i))  ≈⟨ ξ ⟩
            (λ i → (⟦ 𝒜 i ⟧ q) ⟨$⟩ (λ x → (a x) i))  ≈˘⟨ interp-prod 𝒜 q a ⟩
            ⟦ q ⟧₁ ⟨$⟩ a                             ∎
```


An identity satisfied by all algebras in a class is also satisfied by the product
of algebras in the class.


```agda
  ⊧-P-class-invar :  (𝒦 : Pred (Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ)(ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} α))
   →                 𝒦 ⊫ (p ≈̇ q) → (∀ i → 𝒜 i ∈ 𝒦) → ⨅ 𝒜 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)

  ⊧-P-class-invar 𝒦 σ K𝒜 = ⊧-P-invar (λ i ρ → σ .⊫-proof (𝒜 i) (K𝒜 i) ρ)
```


Another fact that will turn out to be useful is that a product of a collection of
algebras models (p ≈̇ q) if the lift of each algebra in the collection models
(p ≈̇ q).


```agda
  ⊧-P-lift-invar : (∀ i → Lift-Algˡ (𝒜 i) β ⊧ (p ≈̇ q))  →  ⨅ 𝒜 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
  ⊧-P-lift-invar α = ⊧-P-invar Aipq
    where
    Aipq : ∀ i → (𝒜 i) ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
    Aipq i = ⊧-lower-invar{𝑨 = (𝒜 i)} p q (α i)
```



#### Modeled identities and homomorphism kernels

If an algebra 𝑨 models an identity (p ≈̇ q), then the pair (p , q) belongs to the
kernel of every homomorphism φ : hom (𝑻 X) 𝑨 from the term algebra to 𝑨; that is,
every homomorphism from 𝑻 X to 𝑨 maps p and q to the same element of 𝑨.

 
```agda
module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥}{X : Type χ}{p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X}{𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ}(φh : hom (𝑻 X) 𝑨) where
  open Setoid (Domain 𝑨) using ( _≈_ )
  private φ = _⟨$⟩_ (proj₁ φh)

  ⊧-H-ker : 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q) → φ p ≈ φ q
  ⊧-H-ker β =
   begin
    φ p                 ≈⟨ cong (proj₁ φh) (term-agreement p)⟩
    φ (⟦ p ⟧ ⟨$⟩ ℊ)     ≈⟨ comm-hom-term φh p ℊ ⟩
    ⟦ p ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (φ ∘ ℊ)  ≈⟨ β (φ ∘ ℊ) ⟩
    ⟦ q ⟧₂ ⟨$⟩ (φ ∘ ℊ)  ≈˘⟨ comm-hom-term φh q ℊ ⟩
    φ (⟦ q ⟧ ⟨$⟩ ℊ)     ≈˘⟨ cong (proj₁ φh) (term-agreement q)⟩
    φ q                 ∎

    where
    open SetoidReasoning (Domain 𝑨)
    open Environment 𝑨      using () renaming ( ⟦_⟧ to ⟦_⟧₂ )
    open Environment (𝑻 X)  using ( ⟦_⟧ )
```

131:##### Derivations in a context
132:
133:`E ⊢ Γ ▹ p ≈ q`{.AgdaDatatype} is the **derivability** relation of equational
134:logic: the equation `p ≈ q`, between terms over the context `Γ`, is derivable from
135:the set of equations `E`.  Its constructors *are* the rules of the logic, and
136:there are only six of them: `hyp`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor} invokes an equation
137:of `E`; `app`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor} is congruence, deriving equality of two
138:applications of an operation symbol from equality of their arguments;
139:`sub`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor} substitutes into a derivation; and
140:`refl`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor}, `sym`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor} and
141:`trans`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor} are the equivalence-relation rules.
142:
143:`⊢▹≈IsEquiv`{.AgdaFunction} packages that last group as an
144:`IsEquivalence`{.AgdaRecord} for derivability in a fixed context, which is what
145:allows derivations to be chained in equational-reasoning style.

148:module _ {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥}{χ ι : Level} where

152:    app    : ∀ {f : OperationSymbolsOf 𝑆}{ps qs}  → (∀ i → E ⊢ Γ ▹ ps i ≈ qs i) → E ⊢ Γ ▹ node f ps ≈ node f qs

163:##### Soundness of the inference rules
164:
165:**Soundness** is the half of the correspondence that says whatever is derivable is
166:true: in any algebra `𝑨` that models every equation of `E`, a derivation of
167:`p ≈ q` yields a proof that `𝑨` satisfies `p ≈ q`.
168:
169:`sound`{.AgdaFunction} is the induction over derivations that establishes it, with
170:one case per rule.  A hypothesis is discharged by the assumption `V` that
171:`𝑨 ⊨ E`; congruence by `cong`{.AgdaField} of the interpretation; substitution by
172:the `substitution`{.AgdaFunction} lemma of [Setoid.Terms.Basic][], which relates a
173:substituted term to the same term under a reinterpreted environment; and the last
174:three rules by the corresponding properties of `𝑨`'s own equality.  The converse,
175:completeness, is proved further down this module.
176:
177:```agda
178:module Soundness
179:  {χ α ι : Level}{I : Type ι} (E : I → Eq {χ = χ})
180:  (𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ)   -- We assume an algebra 𝑨
181:  (V : 𝑨 ⊨ E)          -- that models all equations in E.
182:  where
183:  open Algebra 𝑨 using ( Interp ) --  renaming (Domain to A)
184:
185:  -- In any model 𝑨 that satisfies the equations E, derived equality is actual equality.
186:  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑨 ]
187:  open Environment 𝑨 renaming ( ⟦_⟧s to ⟪_⟫ )
188:  open IsEquivalence renaming ( refl to refl≈ ; sym to  sym≈ ; trans to trans≈ )
189:
190:  sound : ∀ {p q} → E ⊢ X ▹ p ≈ q → 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
191:  sound (hyp i)                    = V i
192:  sound (app {f = f} es) ρ         = Interp .cong (refl , λ i → sound (es i) ρ)
193:  sound (sub {p = p} {q} Epq σ) ρ  = begin
194:    ⟦ p [ σ ] ⟧ ⟨$⟩        ρ  ≈⟨ substitution p σ ρ ⟩
195:    ⟦ p       ⟧ ⟨$⟩ ⟪ σ ⟫  ρ  ≈⟨ sound Epq (⟪ σ ⟫ ρ)  ⟩
196:    ⟦ q       ⟧ ⟨$⟩ ⟪ σ ⟫  ρ  ≈˘⟨ substitution  q σ ρ ⟩
197:    ⟦ q [ σ ] ⟧ ⟨$⟩        ρ  ∎
198:
199:  sound (refl {p = p})                = refl≈   isEquiv {x = p}
200:  sound (sym {p = p} {q} Epq)         = sym≈    isEquiv {x = p}{q}     (sound Epq)
201:  sound (trans{p = p}{q}{r} Epq Eqr)  = trans≈  isEquiv {i = p}{q}{r}  (sound Epq)(sound Eqr)
202:```
203:
204:The deductive closure of a set E is the set of equations modeled by all models of E;
205:that is, `Th Mod E`.
206:
207:The soundness proof above shows
208:
209:    ∀ X → E ⊢ X ▹ p ≈ q → (p , q) ∈ Th Mod ℰ.
210:
211:That is, `∀ X → E ⊢ X ▹ p ≈ q → Mod E ⊫ p ≈ q`.
212:
213:The converse is Birkhoff's completeness theorem:
214:if `Mod E ⊫ p ≈ q`, then `E ⊢ X ▹ p ≈ q`.
215:
216:We will prove that result next.
217:
218:
219:##### Birkhoff's completeness theorem
220:
221:The proof proceeds by constructing a relatively free algebra consisting of term
222:quotiented by derivable equality `E ⊢ X ▹ _≈_`.  It then suffices to prove that this
223:model satisfies all equations in `E`.
224:
225:We denote by `𝔽[ X ]` the *relatively free algebra* over `X` (relative to `E`), which
226:is defined as `Term X` modulo `E ⊢ X ▹ _≈_`.  This algebra `𝔽[ X ]` is "free" or
227:"initial" in the variety of algebras satisfying the identities in `E` in the sense
228:that it satisfies the following universal property: for each algebra `𝑨`, if `𝑨 ⊧ E`,
229:then there is a unique homomorphism from `𝔽[ X ]` to `𝑨`.
230:
231:```agda
232:module FreeAlgebra {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥}{χ : Level}{ι : Level}{I : Type ι}(E : I → Eq {χ = χ}) where
233:  open Algebra
234:
235:  -- Domain of the relatively free algebra.
236:  FreeDomain : Type χ → Setoid _ _
237:  FreeDomain X = record  { Carrier        = Term X
238:                         ; _≈_            = E ⊢ X ▹_≈_
239:                         ; isEquivalence  = ⊢▹≈IsEquiv
240:                         }
241:
242:  -- The interpretation of an operation is simply the operation itself.
243:  -- This works since E ⊢ X ▹_≈_ is a congruence.
244:  FreeInterp : ∀ {X} → (⟨ 𝑆 ⟩ (FreeDomain X)) ⟶ (FreeDomain X)
245:  FreeInterp ⟨$⟩ (f , ts) = node f ts
246:  FreeInterp .cong (refl , h) = app h
247:
248:  -- The relatively free algebra
249:  𝔽[_] : Type χ → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} (ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} χ) (ι ⊔ ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} χ)
250:  Domain 𝔽[ X ] = FreeDomain X
251:  Interp 𝔽[ X ] = FreeInterp
252:
253:  -- The identity substitution σ₀ maps variables to themselves.
254:  σ₀ : {X : Type χ} → Sub {𝑆 = 𝑆} X X
255:  σ₀ x = ℊ x
256:
257:  -- σ₀ acts indeed as identity.
258:  identity : (t : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X) → E ⊢ X ▹ t [ σ₀ ] ≈ t
259:  identity (ℊ x) = refl
260:  identity (node f ts) = app (identity ∘ ts)
261:```
262:
263:Evaluation in the term model is substitution `E ⊢ X ▹ ⟦t⟧σ ≈ t[σ]`. (This would
264:hold "on the nose" if we had function extensionality.)
265:
266:(We put this and the next two lemmas into their own submodules to emphasize
267:the fact that these results are independent of the chosen variable symbol
268:type `X` (or `Δ`, or `Γ`), which is an arbitrary inhabitant of `Type χ`.)
269:
270:```agda
271:  module _ {X : Type χ} where
272:    open Environment 𝔽[ X ]
273:    evaluation : (t : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} Δ) (σ : Sub {𝑆 = 𝑆} X Δ) → E ⊢ X ▹ (⟦ t ⟧ ⟨$⟩ σ) ≈ (t [ σ ])
274:    evaluation (ℊ x) σ = refl
275:    evaluation (node f ts) σ = app (flip (evaluation ∘ ts) σ)
276:
277:  module _ {Δ : Type χ} where
278:    -- The term model satisfies all the equations it started out with.
279:    satisfies : 𝔽[ Δ ] ⊨ E
280:    satisfies i σ = begin
281:      ⟦ p ⟧ ⟨$⟩ σ  ≈⟨ evaluation p σ ⟩
282:      p [ σ ]      ≈⟨ sub (hyp i) σ ⟩
283:      q [ σ ]      ≈˘⟨ evaluation q σ ⟩
284:      ⟦ q ⟧ ⟨$⟩ σ  ∎
285:      where
286:      open Environment 𝔽[ Δ ]
287:      open SetoidReasoning (Domain 𝔽[ Δ ]) ; p = lhs (E i) ; q = rhs (E i)
288:```
289:
290:We are finally ready to formally state and prove Birkhoff's Completeness Theorem,
291:which asserts that every valid consequence is derivable.
292:
293:```agda
294:  module _ {Γ : Type χ} where
295:
296:    completeness : ∀ p q → ModTuple E ⊫ (p ≈̇ q) → E ⊢ Γ ▹ p ≈ q
297:    completeness p q V = begin
298:      p              ≈˘⟨ identity p ⟩
299:      p [ σ₀ ]       ≈˘⟨ evaluation p σ₀ ⟩
300:      ⟦ p ⟧ ⟨$⟩ σ₀   ≈⟨ V .⊫-proof 𝔽[ Γ ] satisfies σ₀ ⟩
301:      ⟦ q ⟧ ⟨$⟩ σ₀   ≈⟨ evaluation q σ₀ ⟩
302:      q [ σ₀ ]       ≈⟨ identity q ⟩
303:      q              ∎
304:      where
305:      open Environment 𝔽[ Γ ]
306:      open SetoidReasoning (Domain 𝔽[ Γ ])
307:```

154:    refl   : ∀ {p : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} Γ}      → E ⊢ Γ ▹ p ≈ p
155:    sym    : ∀ {p q : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} Γ}    → E ⊢ Γ ▹ p ≈ q → E ⊢ Γ ▹ q ≈ p
156:    trans  : ∀ {p q r : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} Γ}  → E ⊢ Γ ▹ p ≈ q → E ⊢ Γ ▹ q ≈ r → E ⊢ Γ ▹ p ≈ r
157:  infix 4 _⊢_▹_≈_
158:
159:  ⊢▹≈IsEquiv : {I : Type ι}{E : I → Eq} → IsEquivalence (E ⊢ Γ ▹_≈_)
160:  ⊢▹≈IsEquiv = record { refl = refl ; sym = sym ; trans = trans }
161:```
162:
163:##### Soundness of the inference rules
164:
165:**Soundness** is the half of the correspondence that says whatever is derivable is
166:true: in any algebra `𝑨` that models every equation of `E`, a derivation of
167:`p ≈ q` yields a proof that `𝑨` satisfies `p ≈ q`.
168:
169:`sound`{.AgdaFunction} is the induction over derivations that establishes it, with
170:one case per rule.  A hypothesis is discharged by the assumption `V` that
171:`𝑨 ⊨ E`; congruence by `cong`{.AgdaField} of the interpretation; substitution by
172:the `substitution`{.AgdaFunction} lemma of [Setoid.Terms.Basic][], which relates a
173:substituted term to the same term under a reinterpreted environment; and the last
174:three rules by the corresponding properties of `𝑨`'s own equality.  The converse,
175:completeness, is proved further down this module.
176:
177:```agda
178:module Soundness
179:  {χ α ι : Level}{I : Type ι} (E : I → Eq {χ = χ})
180:  (𝑨 : Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} α ρᵃ)   -- We assume an algebra 𝑨
181:  (V : 𝑨 ⊨ E)          -- that models all equations in E.
182:  where
183:  open Algebra 𝑨 using ( Interp ) --  renaming (Domain to A)
184:
185:  -- In any model 𝑨 that satisfies the equations E, derived equality is actual equality.
186:  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑨 ]
187:  open Environment 𝑨 renaming ( ⟦_⟧s to ⟪_⟫ )
188:  open IsEquivalence renaming ( refl to refl≈ ; sym to  sym≈ ; trans to trans≈ )
189:
190:  sound : ∀ {p q} → E ⊢ X ▹ p ≈ q → 𝑨 ⊧ (p ≈̇ q)
191:  sound (hyp i)                    = V i
192:  sound (app {f = f} es) ρ         = Interp .cong (refl , λ i → sound (es i) ρ)
193:  sound (sub {p = p} {q} Epq σ) ρ  = begin
194:    ⟦ p [ σ ] ⟧ ⟨$⟩        ρ  ≈⟨ substitution p σ ρ ⟩
195:    ⟦ p       ⟧ ⟨$⟩ ⟪ σ ⟫  ρ  ≈⟨ sound Epq (⟪ σ ⟫ ρ)  ⟩
196:    ⟦ q       ⟧ ⟨$⟩ ⟪ σ ⟫  ρ  ≈˘⟨ substitution  q σ ρ ⟩
197:    ⟦ q [ σ ] ⟧ ⟨$⟩        ρ  ∎
198:
199:  sound (refl {p = p})                = refl≈   isEquiv {x = p}
200:  sound (sym {p = p} {q} Epq)         = sym≈    isEquiv {x = p}{q}     (sound Epq)
201:  sound (trans{p = p}{q}{r} Epq Eqr)  = trans≈  isEquiv {i = p}{q}{r}  (sound Epq)(sound Eqr)
202:```
203:
204:The deductive closure of a set E is the set of equations modeled by all models of E;
205:that is, `Th Mod E`.
206:
207:The soundness proof above shows
208:
209:    ∀ X → E ⊢ X ▹ p ≈ q → (p , q) ∈ Th Mod ℰ.
210:
211:That is, `∀ X → E ⊢ X ▹ p ≈ q → Mod E ⊫ p ≈ q`.
212:
213:The converse is Birkhoff's completeness theorem:
214:if `Mod E ⊫ p ≈ q`, then `E ⊢ X ▹ p ≈ q`.
215:
216:We will prove that result next.
217:
218:
219:##### Birkhoff's completeness theorem
220:
221:The proof proceeds by constructing a relatively free algebra consisting of term
222:quotiented by derivable equality `E ⊢ X ▹ _≈_`.  It then suffices to prove that this
223:model satisfies all equations in `E`.
224:
225:We denote by `𝔽[ X ]` the *relatively free algebra* over `X` (relative to `E`), which
226:is defined as `Term X` modulo `E ⊢ X ▹ _≈_`.  This algebra `𝔽[ X ]` is "free" or
227:"initial" in the variety of algebras satisfying the identities in `E` in the sense
228:that it satisfies the following universal property: for each algebra `𝑨`, if `𝑨 ⊧ E`,
229:then there is a unique homomorphism from `𝔽[ X ]` to `𝑨`.
230:
231:```agda
232:module FreeAlgebra {𝑆 : Signature 𝓞 𝓥}{χ : Level}{ι : Level}{I : Type ι}(E : I → Eq {χ = χ}) where
233:  open Algebra
234:
235:  -- Domain of the relatively free algebra.
236:  FreeDomain : Type χ → Setoid _ _
237:  FreeDomain X = record  { Carrier        = Term X
238:                         ; _≈_            = E ⊢ X ▹_≈_
239:                         ; isEquivalence  = ⊢▹≈IsEquiv
240:                         }
241:
242:  -- The interpretation of an operation is simply the operation itself.
243:  -- This works since E ⊢ X ▹_≈_ is a congruence.
244:  FreeInterp : ∀ {X} → (⟨ 𝑆 ⟩ (FreeDomain X)) ⟶ (FreeDomain X)
245:  FreeInterp ⟨$⟩ (f , ts) = node f ts
246:  FreeInterp .cong (refl , h) = app h
247:
248:  -- The relatively free algebra
249:  𝔽[_] : Type χ → Algebra {𝑆 = 𝑆} (ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} χ) (ι ⊔ ov {𝑆 = 𝑆} χ)
250:  Domain 𝔽[ X ] = FreeDomain X
251:  Interp 𝔽[ X ] = FreeInterp
252:
253:  -- The identity substitution σ₀ maps variables to themselves.
254:  σ₀ : {X : Type χ} → Sub {𝑆 = 𝑆} X X
255:  σ₀ x = ℊ x
256:
257:  -- σ₀ acts indeed as identity.
258:  identity : (t : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} X) → E ⊢ X ▹ t [ σ₀ ] ≈ t
259:  identity (ℊ x) = refl
260:  identity (node f ts) = app (identity ∘ ts)
261:```
262:
263:Evaluation in the term model is substitution `E ⊢ X ▹ ⟦t⟧σ ≈ t[σ]`. (This would
264:hold "on the nose" if we had function extensionality.)
265:
266:(We put this and the next two lemmas into their own submodules to emphasize
267:the fact that these results are independent of the chosen variable symbol
268:type `X` (or `Δ`, or `Γ`), which is an arbitrary inhabitant of `Type χ`.)
269:
270:```agda
271:  module _ {X : Type χ} where
272:    open Environment 𝔽[ X ]
273:    evaluation : (t : Term {𝑆 = 𝑆} Δ) (σ : Sub {𝑆 = 𝑆} X Δ) → E ⊢ X ▹ (⟦ t ⟧ ⟨$⟩ σ) ≈ (t [ σ ])
274:    evaluation (ℊ x) σ = refl
275:    evaluation (node f ts) σ = app (flip (evaluation ∘ ts) σ)
276:
277:  module _ {Δ : Type χ} where
278:    -- The term model satisfies all the equations it started out with.
279:    satisfies : 𝔽[ Δ ] ⊨ E
280:    satisfies i σ = begin
281:      ⟦ p ⟧ ⟨$⟩ σ  ≈⟨ evaluation p σ ⟩
282:      p [ σ ]      ≈⟨ sub (hyp i) σ ⟩
283:      q [ σ ]      ≈˘⟨ evaluation q σ ⟩
284:      ⟦ q ⟧ ⟨$⟩ σ  ∎
285:      where
286:      open Environment 𝔽[ Δ ]
287:      open SetoidReasoning (Domain 𝔽[ Δ ]) ; p = lhs (E i) ; q = rhs (E i)
288:```
289:
290:We are finally ready to formally state and prove Birkhoff's Completeness Theorem,
291:which asserts that every valid consequence is derivable.
292:
293:```agda
294:  module _ {Γ : Type χ} where
295:
296:    completeness : ∀ p q → ModTuple E ⊫ (p ≈̇ q) → E ⊢ Γ ▹ p ≈ q
297:    completeness p q V = begin
298:      p              ≈˘⟨ identity p ⟩
299:      p [ σ₀ ]       ≈˘⟨ evaluation p σ₀ ⟩
300:      ⟦ p ⟧ ⟨$⟩ σ₀   ≈⟨ V .⊫-proof 𝔽[ Γ ] satisfies σ₀ ⟩
301:      ⟦ q ⟧ ⟨$⟩ σ₀   ≈⟨ evaluation q σ₀ ⟩
302:      q [ σ₀ ]       ≈⟨ identity q ⟩
303:      q              ∎
304:      where
305:      open Environment 𝔽[ Γ ]
306:      open SetoidReasoning (Domain 𝔽[ Γ ])
307:```
